title: ADSR
text: ADSR ADSR in the module view Introduction The ADSR is the classic envelope generator: attack, decay, sustain, release . A gate starts it and it draws one shape over time. That shape opens a VCA so a note gets loud and fades, or sweeps a filter's cutoff. It also has an Active output that stays high while the envelope is running. Inside a Voice Cell this tells the cell when a voice has gone quiet and can be reused. How does it work? The envelope moves through four stages: Attack: when the Gate goes high, the level rises in a straight line to its peak. The rise starts at the current level, not at zero, so retriggering a note that is still sounding doesn't click. Decay: the level falls to the sustain level along an exponential curve. Sustain: the level holds there for as long as the gate stays high. Release: when the gate goes low, the level falls exponentially to silence. When the release reaches −80 dB, the envelope stops, End fires one trigger and Active goes low. The peak depends on velocity. With Vel Amount at 0 % every note peaks at 1.0. At 100 % the peak equals the Velocity input, so soft notes stay quiet. Sustain is a share of that peak: a soft note sustains lower than a loud one. A trigger at Retrigger while the gate is high restarts the attack from the current level. Use it for repeated accents within one long note. How to use it? Amplitude envelope: patch Gate from a Voice In (or a sequencer's gate), Env onto a VCA's Gain knob. Since Gain starts at 0, the envelope opens it completely. In a Voice Cell: also patch Active into Voice Out › Active . The cell then frees the voice exactly when its sound has faded, and not while the release is still audible. Filter envelope: patch Env onto a filter's Cutoff knob and set the cable's amount. Use a short decay and a low sustain for a plucky sound. Velocity: patch Velocity from Voice In and raise Vel Amount . Chaining: End fires when the release is done. Patch it into another envelope's gate or a Function's Trig to start the next event. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Attack 1 ms – 10 s 5 ms Decay 1 ms – 10 s 300 ms Sustain 0 – 100 % 70 % Release 1 ms – 20 s 400 ms Vel Amount 0 – 100 % 50 % Attack: how long the rise from silence to the peak takes. The rise is linear, so short attacks stay punchy. The knob's centre is 200 ms; the lower half gives fine control over short times. Decay: time to fall from the peak to the sustain level. The curve is exponential and gets close to the target after the set time. The centre is 400 ms. Sustain: the level held while the gate stays high, as a share of the peak. At 0 % the envelope decays to silence even with the gate held: a percussive shape. At 100 % there is no decay. Release: time from the gate going low to silence (−80 dB). The centre is 600 ms. A gate that ends during the attack or decay starts the release from wherever the level is. Vel Amount: how much velocity lowers the peak. Peak = 1 − Vel Amount × (1 − Velocity). At 0 % velocity is ignored; at 100 % a velocity of 0.3 gives a peak of 0.3. Every knob is a modulation destination: patch a cable onto it to move it. Inputs Input Signal What it does Gate gate high (≥ 0.5) starts the attack; low starts the release Retrigger trigger while the gate is high, restarts the attack from the current level Velocity control, 0 – 1 scales the peak through Vel Amount ; unpatched counts as full velocity Outputs Output Signal What it does Env control, 0 – 1 the envelope End trigger one pulse when the release reaches silence Active gate high from the first attack until the release has finished

title: Segments
text: Segments Segments in the module view Introduction Segments draws any envelope you like out of up to eight pieces. Each piece (a segment ) is a ramp, a step or a hold with its own time, level and curve. Chain four of them and you have an ADSR; add a hold and it's an AHDSR; add a second peak and it's a swell that breathes twice. Mark some segments as a loop and the chain keeps cycling through them: an LFO of any shape you can draw, or an envelope whose sustain wobbles. Each segment has a gate output that is high while it runs, and a trigger input that can end it or jump to it, so segments can wait for events and announce when they play. Where ADSR is fixed to four stages and Function is one rise and one fall, Segments is the general case, edited by dragging points on a graph. How does it work? Segment types Every segment starts from wherever the output is when it begins, so jumps and retriggers never click. Ramp moves to its Level over its Time . Shape bends it: 0 is straight, +1 exponential (a slow start rising, a quick drop falling: the snappy feel of an analog envelope), −1 the opposite. Step jumps to its Level and stays there for its Time . With Shape above 0, it glides there over that share of the time instead. A few steps in a loop make a little stepped sequence. Hold keeps the level it starts with. Its Wait decides when it ends: after its Time ; while the Gate is high (a sustain); or at the next pulse on its Seg input (or when the Gate falls). Time runs from 0.5 ms to 30 s; Time Scale multiplies every time at once, so patching velocity or pitch onto it makes the whole envelope faster or slower. Modulating a Time knob bends the segment while it plays. Gates, loops and release Gate rising: the chain starts again at segment 1, from the current level. Active goes high, and Velocity is read: with Vel Amount up, softer notes reach lower levels. The loop: the segments from the first to the last with Loop on. After the last loop segment the chain goes back to the first and Loop fires. A single looped Ramp restarts from the level before it each time: a saw. The sustain point is the last Hold that waits for the Gate, or else the end of the loop. Everything after it is the release . Gate falling , Release = Jump : if the chain hasn't passed the sustain point yet, it jumps straight to the release, from the current level, like any envelope whose key is let go early. Release = Finish : the loop completes its pass and the earlier segments play out, then the release follows. Without a sustain point or a loop the chain is a one-shot: how long the gate stays high doesn't matter. End fires when the last segment finishes; the output stays at its level and Active falls. Seg 1 … 8 inputs. With Seg In on Advance , a pulse ends that segment if it's running (whatever its type). With Jump , a pulse makes the chain jump to that segment from wherever it is. The Seg outputs are high while their segment runs, exactly one at a time. Free running and sync Run = Free starts the chain on its own (and again at every transport start): with a loop it's an LFO, without one a single sweep. A rising Gate still restarts it. Sync turns each segment's time into a note value (8 bars … 1/64T, straight, dotted and triplet), chosen in the segment's row. With Run = Free and the transport playing, the chain is locked to the song: the part before the loop plays from the transport start, and the loop sits on the bar grid, so it is at the same place in every bar, survives loop jumps and renders the same every time. (Holds then last their note value too.) A Gate or Seg pulse unlocks it until the next transport start; when the transport stops it keeps running at the current tempo. The editor The graph shows the chain; each segment's width grows with its time. Drag a point up and down for the segment's Level , left and right for its Time (with Sync, through the note values). Drag a curve up and down for its Shape . Click a segment to select it. Its row below sets Type , Wait (holds), Loop , Seg In and the note value (with Sync), and shows its three knobs, with their modulation rings and cables. Drag across the strip at the top to set the loop region; click a lone looped segment there to clear the loop. − / + change the number of segments; Templates rewrites the chain as an AD, ADSR, AHDSR, two-peak swell, ramp or triangle LFO, a 4- or 8-step loop, or a gated burst (one undo step). A dot follows the output, and the running segment's label lights up. How to use it? Envelope with a hold: Templates › AHDSR, Gate from a sequencer or Voice In , Out onto a VCA, Active into Voice Out › Active . Pluck with a second bloom: Templates › Swell, Run Gated, onto a filter. Custom LFO: Templates › Triangle LFO, then drag the points: a lopsided, curved wave. Turn Sync on for a tempo-locked shape. Stepped sequence: Templates › 8-step loop, Sync on, each step 1/16: Out onto a quantizer, Seg outputs as triggers for drums. Wait for the beat: set a Hold to Wait: Trigger and patch a clock into its Seg input: the envelope pauses there until the next beat. Swell and burst: Templates › Gated burst: a pulsing attack while the key is held, then a smooth release. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Segments does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Segments under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Segments: Two-Bloom Pluck Five segments draw an attack, a drop, a second bloom, a sustain hold and a release on the VCA and filter. Segments: Lopsided LFO Four looped segments with Sync and Run Free make a tempo-locked LFO with a shape of your own on a bass filter. Segments: Step Melody Eight Step segments of 1/8 each act as a sequencer; the Levels are pitches, quantized to a scale. Segments: Breathing Pad A two-peak swell with a gate-waiting Hold ; Time Scale stretches the whole breath. Segments: Drums From Segments Eight looped Step segments form a one-bar clock; the Seg outputs trigger the drums and Out moves a bass filter. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Time 1 … 8 0.5 ms – 30 s 5 ms, 300 ms, 250 ms, 400 ms, then 250 ms Level 1 … 8 −1 … +1 1.0, 0.7, 0, 0, then 0 Shape 1 … 8 −1 … +1 0, +0.5, 0, +0.5, then 0 Time Scale ×0.1 – ×10 ×1 Vel Amount 0 – 100 % 0 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Count 1 – 8 4 Run Gated, Free Gated Release Jump, Finish Jump Sync Off, On Off Per segment (in the editor): Type (Ramp, Step, Hold), Loop, Wait (Time, Gate, Trigger; holds only), Seg In (Advance, Jump) and the note value used with Sync (1/4 by default). A new module is an ADSR: Ramp, Ramp, Hold (Gate), Ramp. Inputs Input Signal What it does Gate gate starts the chain; falling, goes to the release Velocity control scales the levels through Vel Amount (unpatched: full) Seg 1 … 8 trigger ends that segment ( Advance ) or jumps to it ( Jump ) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the chain Inv control the chain upside down Seg 1 … 8 gate high while that segment runs Loop trigger a new loop pass starts End trigger the last segment finished Active gate from the start until End

title: Shape Env
text: Shape Env Shape Env in the module view Introduction Shape Env is an envelope and LFO that plays shapes from a library instead of building them from stages. There are 96 ready-made shapes (percussive decays, plucks, swells, sustained envelopes, bounces, stairs, rhythmic gates, classic and unusual LFO waves, organic textures) and 8 slots for shapes you draw yourself. Pick a shape, set how long it takes, and trigger it: a one-shot envelope. Hold a gate and it waits at the shape's sustain point. Loop it and it's an LFO. Shapes that no attack-decay-sustain-release could ever make (echoing bounces, stutters, irregular gates) are one click away. How does it work? Choosing. Shape picks one of 104: 0–95 are the library, 96–103 your own ( User 1 … 8 ). The knob shows the shape's name. Browse opens a grid of thumbnails grouped by family; hover one to see it big, click to choose it. With the view focused, ← and → step through the shapes. Morph blends the shape into its neighbour in the list. Neighbours are related (Short exp → Long exp, Bounce 5 → Bounce 8), so Morph moves smoothly between them; across a family boundary it blends unlike shapes, which can be fun too. Time is how long the whole shape takes (1 ms – 60 s), or one cycle in Loop. With Sync it's a note value instead. Skew warps time without changing the length: + plays the start faster and the end slower (at +1 the first half takes a quarter of the time), − the other way. Reverse plays the shape backwards. Level scales the output, and Vel Amount lets the Velocity input scale it: at 0 % every start is full level, at 100 % the level follows the velocity. Velocity is read at each start. Modes One-shot: Trig or a rising Gate plays the whole shape once; End fires at the end and the output stays at the last value (0 for envelopes). A new start while it plays restarts it with a 2 ms crossfade (no click), or, with Retrigger on Ignore , is ignored until it's done. Gated: like One-shot, but while the Gate is high the shape waits at its sustain point (the dashed line in the preview), and plays the rest when the gate falls. A short gate that ends before the sustain point just plays through. Shapes without a sustain point behave as One-shot; Trig starts the shape like a very short gate. Loop: the shape repeats every Time ; End fires at each wrap. Trig or Gate restart it (crossfaded). Envelope shapes loop too: a repeating decay is a classic rhythmic effect. With Sync and the transport playing, the loop is locked to the song position: always at the same place in the bar, after loop jumps too, and every render is the same. In One-shot and Gated a new Shape is picked up at the next start; in Loop it crossfades over 5 ms. Morph works at any time. Phase outputs where the playback is (0 … 1): a ramp for other modules. Active is high while the shape plays (always in Loop). Inv is the upside down shape ( 1 − Out , or −Out for bipolar shapes). Drawing your own Select a user slot ( User 1 … 8 ) and press Draw . Drag to draw freehand, or choose Line to drag straight segments. Smooth softens the drawing, Mirror makes it symmetric, Snap 8 / 16 turns it into steps. Sustain lets you click where Gated mode should wait ( No sustain removes it). Envelope / Cycle decides whether the shape loops seamlessly (a cycle ends where it starts), ± Bipolar whether it spans −1 … +1. On a library shape, Copy to puts the shape as you see it (with Morph, Skew and Reverse) into a user slot, ready to be changed. Every stroke is one undo step. Drawn shapes are saved with the board. How to use it? Percussive accents: Decays or Plucks, Time 200 ms, One-shot, triggered by a sequencer, onto a VCA. Echoing gate: Bounces › Echoes 1/8 , Sync 1/2, triggered on the beat: a VCA that echoes the note. Rhythmic chopper: Gates family, Loop, Sync 1 bar, onto a VCA: a trance gate. Morph between two patterns for variations. Pad envelope in a Voice Cell: Sustains › Pad , Gated, Gate from Voice In , Active into Voice Out › Active . Breathing LFO: Wobbles › Breathing , Loop, Time 4 s, onto a filter. Your own groove: draw a shape in User 1 , Snap 16, Loop, Sync 1 bar: a step-like modulation drawn in seconds. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Shape Env does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Shape Env under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Shape Env: Pluck Morph A Pluck shape in One-shot mode on every note, with a slow LFO on Morph between neighbouring shapes. Shape Env: Gate Pattern A rhythmic shape in Loop mode with Sync 1/1 chops a chord into a gate pattern; Morph varies it. Shape Env: Echoing Bell The Echoes 1/8 shape repeats each bell note on the beat grid with no delay effect. Shape Env: Breathing Filter The Breathing shape in Loop mode opens a filter while Inv closes another one. Shape Env: Synth Drums Short exp as pitch drop, Pluck as amplitude and Roll on a noise snare build drums from sine oscillators. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Time 1 ms – 60 s 500 ms Shape 104 shapes (96 library, 8 user) Click Morph 0 – 100 % 0 % Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Vel Amount 0 – 100 % 0 % Skew −1 … +1 0 Every knob is a modulation destination (a cable on Shape steps through the library). Settings Setting Values Default Mode One-shot, Gated, Loop One-shot Sync Off, 16 bars … 1/32T (straight, dotted, triplet) Off Reverse Off, On Off Retrigger (One-shot, Gated) Restart, Ignore Restart Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig trigger starts the shape Gate gate starts the shape; in Gated mode holds it at the sustain point while high Velocity control scales the level through Vel Amount (unpatched: full) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the shape Inv control the shape upside down Phase control the playback position, 0 … 1 End trigger the shape finished (or wrapped, in Loop) Active gate the shape is playing

title: Function
text: Function Function in the module view Introduction The Function is a slope generator : it rises to 1 and falls back to 0. That one gesture covers a lot of jobs. Left running in a loop it's an LFO. Started by a trigger it's an attack/decay envelope. It can lock to Live's tempo. Its four outputs are related copies of the same slope, shifted in phase or stretched in time, so one module can move several things in a coordinated way. How does it work? Each cycle has two parts: a rise from 0 to 1 that takes Rise seconds and a fall back to 0 that takes Fall seconds. Shape bends both slopes: straight at 0, exponential toward +1, logarithmic toward −1. The view draws the resulting slope live. Cycle on (LFO). The slope repeats. One cycle lasts Rise + Fall , so equal values give a triangle and lopsided values give a ramp or a saw. A rising edge at Trig restarts the cycle from the beginning (hard reset). EOC fires at the end of every cycle. Cycle off (envelope). The Function waits. A rising edge at Trig starts the rise from wherever the output is, then the fall follows on its own. How long the trigger stays high doesn't matter. EOC fires when output A has fallen back to 0. Sync. With a note value selected, the cycle (or the whole envelope) lasts exactly that long at the current tempo. Rise and Fall then only set the proportion between rise and fall, not the time. While Live's transport is playing, a cycling Function is locked to the song position, so it lines up with the bar wherever you start playback. With the transport stopped it runs at the tempo without the lock. Starting the transport always restarts it. Spread derives outputs B, C and D from A: Cycling: B, C and D are shifted in phase by Spread × ¼ cycle each. At 100 % the four outputs are a quarter cycle apart (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°). Envelope: B, C and D take longer, each by a factor of (1 + Spread) more than the one before. At 100 % B is twice as long as A, C four times and D eight times. At 0 % Spread all four outputs are identical. How to use it? LFO: leave Cycle on, set Rise and Fall , and patch A onto any knob, e.g. a filter's cutoff. Set the depth with the cable's amount. Tempo-synced LFO: choose a Sync value such as 1/4 or 1 bar. Set Rise short and Fall long for a ramp down on every beat. Envelope: turn Cycle off and patch a gate or trigger into Trig . Short rise and longer fall gives a pluck; Shape toward +1 makes it snappier. Movement across several voices or parameters: with Spread up, patch A, B, C and D to four different destinations. They move together but not in lockstep: four phases of one LFO, or four envelopes of growing length. Sequencing events: EOC fires once per cycle or at the end of the envelope. Use it as a clock for Random or to trigger another envelope. Self-cycling with a twist: with Cycle off, patch EOC back into Trig . It loops, and you can patch other triggers in as well. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Rise 1 ms – 10 s 250 ms Fall 1 ms – 10 s 250 ms Shape −1 … +1 0 (linear) Spread 0 – 100 % 0 % Cycle on / off on Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars Free Rise: duration of the rising part. Its knob centre is 250 ms. In sync mode only the ratio Rise : Fall counts. Fall: duration of the falling part, same range. With Cycle on, the frequency is 1 / (Rise + Fall): 250 ms + 250 ms = 2 Hz. Shape: the curve of both slopes. 0 is linear. Positive values are exponential: the rise starts slowly and speeds up, the fall drops fast and then eases out. This is the punchy, natural-sounding envelope. Negative values are logarithmic, the other way round: the rise shoots up and settles, the fall lingers and then drops away. Spread: how far B, C and D differ from A. Phase offsets when cycling, longer durations as an envelope (see above). Cycle: on loops the slope (LFO); off makes a one-shot envelope started by Trig . Sync: Free uses the times from Rise and Fall . A note value fixes the total length to that note at Live's tempo (4/4 assumed). Rise and Fall then share that time in their ratio. Rise , Fall , Shape and Spread are modulation destinations. Modulating Rise or Fall from another Function gives an LFO with a wandering rate. Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig gate rising edge: restarts the cycle (Cycle on) or starts the envelope (Cycle off) Outputs Output Signal What it does A control, 0 – 1 the slope B control, 0 – 1 A shifted ¼ × Spread in phase, or stretched by (1 + Spread) C control, 0 – 1 shifted ½ × Spread, or stretched by (1 + Spread)² D control, 0 – 1 shifted ¾ × Spread, or stretched by (1 + Spread)³ EOC trigger end of cycle: once per loop, or when A's envelope finishes

title: Six Slopes
text: Six Slopes Six Slopes in the module view Introduction Six Slopes is six slope generators on one set of knobs . Each slope rises and falls; together they can be six envelopes, six LFOs or, at audio rate, six oscillators that form a chord of harmonics. The trick is the Harmonics knob. In the middle all six run at the same speed. Turn it right and they spread out over the overtone series (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 times as fast); turn it left and they slow down over the undertones (½, ⅓ … ⅙). In between, the speeds are uneven, so looping slopes drift in and out of phase: slow, shifting patterns from one knob. How does it work? One slope. Rate sets how fast channel 1 runs; Skew is the share of the slope spent rising (25 %: a quick rise and a longer fall), and Curve bends it: −1 logarithmic, 0 straight, +1 exponential. The Pitch input adds octaves to the rate of all six. Six speeds. Each channel runs at channel 1's rate times its ratio. With Harmonics at +1 the ratios are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: channel 6 is six times as fast, so its envelope is six times as short. At −1 they're 1, ½, ⅓, ¼, ⅕, ⅙. Snap rounds the ratios: Integer snaps to whole numbers (or whole-number fractions to the left), so the knob steps through whole-number chords: at 0.4 the ratios are 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3. Just snaps each ratio to the nearest note of a just scale (1, 9/8, 5/4, 4/3, 3/2, 5/3, 15/8, in any octave): in Sound mode, six notes of a pure, beatless chord. The lane next to each slope shows its current ratio as a fraction (or the note it plays in Sound mode). Shared triggers. Every channel has its own Trig input. An unpatched Trig listens to the nearest patched one above it, so one gate into Trig 1 starts all six, and with Harmonics up the six envelopes end one after another, a natural "strum" of decays. Patch Trig 4 too, and channels 4–6 follow it while 1–3 still follow Trig 1 . Modes AR: a one-shot envelope per trigger. The rise starts from wherever the level is, so a retrigger during the fall never jumps. ASR: rises while the gate is high, holds at the top, falls when the gate goes low (from wherever it is, even during the rise). Loop: six LFOs. A Trig rising edge restarts that channel's cycle. With nothing patched they run freely, all starting together. Sound: six oscillators. Rate now spans 16 Hz – 4 kHz with C4 in the middle; Skew moves the wave from saw to triangle to ramp and Curve bends it (+0.5 is close to a sine). A Trig edge hard-syncs its channel. Partials above a quarter of the sample rate fade out instead of aliasing. Sync (AR, ASR, Loop) makes channel 1's slope one note value long at the current tempo; the others keep their ratios. In Loop with the transport playing every channel is locked to the song position, so with whole-number ratios they meet again on every note value, after loop jumps too, and every render is the same. Pitch then shifts in whole octaves. Levels and Sum Level scales all six. Tilt balances them: at +1 channel 1 is silent and channel 6 at full level, at −1 the other way round (a darker chord in Sound mode, as with natural overtones). Sum mixes the six: six unipolar slopes reach full scale when about half of them are up. In Loop it's a complex, slowly changing contour; in Sound mode it's the mixed tone, gently limited. End 1 fires when channel 1 finishes its slope or cycle. Active is high while any channel moves (AR, ASR) and always in Loop and Sound. How to use it? Strummed decays: a sequencer gate into Trig 1 , AR, Skew 5 %, Harmonics +0.6; patch the six outputs to six VCAs or filter cutoffs. Six-part rhythm envelopes: six drum triggers into the six Trigs, one envelope each, with one set of shape knobs. Phasing LFOs: Loop, Harmonics at a small, uneven value like 0.13: six slow waves that drift apart and back. Sum onto a filter for a contour that never quite repeats. Polyrhythm on the grid: Loop, Sync 1 bar, Snap Integer, Harmonics +1: six LFOs at 1–6 cycles per bar, locked to the song. A just chord: Sound, Snap Just, Pitch from Voice In › Pitch , Sum into a VCA. Turn Harmonics for different chords and Tilt to the left for a softer tone. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Six Slopes does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Six Slopes under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Six Slopes: Strummed Chord One trigger on Trig 1 in AR with Harmonics at +0.6 and a short Skew : six notes open one after another like a strum. Six Slopes: Phasing Pulses Loop mode with a small Harmonics value: six slow swells drift apart and back over a chord. Six Slopes: Bar Polyrhythm Loop , Sync on one bar and Snap on Integer: six slopes at one to six cycles per bar, locked to the song. Six Slopes: Six-Part Percussion Six drum triggers fire six slopes, each shaping a different sine tone; one Skew and Curve set shapes all decays. Six Slopes: Just Drone Sound mode with Snap on Just and the sequencer on Pitch : six oscillators in pure ratios, moved by an LFO on Harmonics . Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 0.02–1000 Hz (shown as 50 s – 1 ms); Sound: 16 Hz – 4 kHz 2 Hz (500 ms) Harmonics −1 … +1 0 Skew 0 – 100 % 25 % Curve −1 … +1 0 Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Tilt −1 … +1 0 Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Mode AR, ASR, Loop, Sound AR Snap Off, Integer, Just Off Sync (not in Sound) Free, 8 bars … 1/32T Free Polarity (Loop) Unipolar, Bipolar Unipolar Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig 1 … Trig 6 gate starts, holds, restarts or syncs its channel; unpatched, follows the nearest patched Trig above Pitch pitch added to Rate in octaves Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 … Out 6 control each channel's slope Sum control the six mixed End 1 trigger channel 1 finished its slope or cycle Active gate a channel is moving (always high in Loop and Sound)

title: Tidal
text: Tidal Tidal in the module view Introduction Tidal is a slope generator : a voltage that rises and falls, again and again. Slow, it's a swell that takes minutes; medium, it's an LFO; fast, it's a tone you can hear. Trigger it and it becomes an envelope. One knob, Skew , decides how the cycle is split between rising and falling, Curve bends the slopes, and Smooth either rounds everything into a sine-like curve or folds it into a bright, many-peaked contour. Four outputs carry four related versions of the same slope, so one Tidal can move four things in a pattern that belongs together. How does it work? One cycle is a rise and a fall. Frequency sets how many cycles per second; Range picks the knob's span: Slow (one cycle per 1000 s up to 1 Hz), Medium (0.02–50 Hz) or Audio (8 Hz – 8 kHz, C4 at the centre). The Pitch input adds octaves (1 V/oct), so in the Audio range Tidal plays in tune. Skew is the share of the cycle spent rising. At 50 % it's a triangle; at 0 % a falling saw, at 100 % a rising saw. The total time stays the same. In the Audio range Skew stops just short of the ends, so the wave never jumps vertically. Curve bends both slopes: −1 logarithmic (quick start, slow arrival), 0 straight, +0.5 a round cosine (a sine-like wave at Skew 50 %), +1 exponential (slow start, quick arrival). Smooth below 0 passes each output through a gentle low-pass that follows the cycle rate: at −1 every shape becomes an almost pure sine, and Tidal restores its full level once per cycle so the swing doesn't shrink. Above 0 it folds : the slope is amplified and mirrored back into range each time it hits an edge. At +1 a triangle turns into seven peaks per cycle: busy contours at LFO rates, rich tones at audio rate. Modes Loop: cycles all the time. A rising edge on Trig restarts the cycle. AD: waits at 0. A rising edge on Trig plays one rise and one fall, then End fires. A new trigger during the fall rises again from where the level is, without a jump. AR: rises while Trig is high, holds at the top, and falls when it goes low, from wherever the level is. Rise time is Skew ÷ Frequency, fall time the rest. AD and AR are always unipolar (0 … 1). In Loop, Polarity chooses −1 … +1 or 0 … 1. The four outputs A is the main slope. B , C and D follow it as Relation says, and Spread sets how far apart they are (at 0 all four are the same): Phase: each output is shifted along the cycle. At +1 the four are a quarter cycle apart (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); negative Spread shifts the other way. In AD/AR the envelopes start one after another instead, a quarter of the slope's length apart at ±1. Level: the outputs get quieter: B at two thirds, C at a third, D at nothing for Spread ±1. Below 0, B and D are also upside down: a fan that alternates. Ratio: rhythmic ratios that come back together. Spread picks a set (the knob shows it): 2 · 3 · 4, then 3/2 · 2 · 3, 4/3 · 3/2 · 2, 5/4 · 3/2 · 7/4, 5/3 · 7/4 · 9/4, faster on the right, the slower reciprocals on the left. All four restart together whenever their pattern repeats (for 4/3 · 3/2 · 2: every 6 cycles of A). Harmonic: frequency ratios. At +1 B, C and D run 2, 3 and 4 times as fast as A (overtones), at −1 at ½, ⅓ and ¼ (undertones). In between the ratios are uneven and the outputs slowly drift against each other. In AD and AR, Ratio and Harmonic change each output's length instead: an output at ratio 2 is an envelope half as long. One trigger, four accents. Timing Free: Frequency and Pitch, modulated every sample (smooth FM). Sync: one cycle per note value (1/32T … 8 bars). While the transport plays, the cycle is locked to the song position: always at the same point at the same bar, even after a loop jump, and the Ratio and Harmonic outputs lock with it. Pitch still shifts the speed in whole octaves (+1: two cycles per note value). Clock: patch a clock into Clock and Tidal measures its tempo (averaging the last four pulses) and runs at Ratio × the clock. For ×2 and faster the cycle restarts on every pulse, for ÷2 and slower on every n-th pulse, so it stays in step. After a pause the measurement starts again instead of jumping to a wild rate. The Frequency knob then shows the ratio and the measured BPM. Clock wins over Sync, Sync over Frequency. Rise is high while A rises. End fires when A finishes a cycle (Loop) or reaches 0 (AD, AR). Both come from A before smoothing, so they're on time even when Smooth delays the curve. How to use it? Slow swell: Range Slow , Frequency to a few minutes per cycle, A onto a filter's cutoff. Skew 80 % for long rises and quicker falls. Circular motion: Relation Phase , Spread +1, Curve +0.5: A and B are a sine and a cosine. Patch them to two pans, or A to a filter and C (the opposite) to a reverb send. Polyrhythm: Relation Ratio , Sync 1 bar, Spread at 4/3 · 3/2 · 2: four modulations that meet again every six bars. Accent pattern: Mode AD , Relation Harmonic , Spread +1, one trigger from a sequencer: four envelopes of four lengths onto four VCAs. Oscillator: Range Audio , Pitch from a sequencer or Voice In › Pitch , A into a VCA's audio input. Turn Skew for saw-to-triangle, Smooth up for folded overtones, down for a pure sine. Clocked LFO: a sequencer's clock into Clock , Ratio ÷4: one cycle per bar that follows tempo changes and a manual clock. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Tidal does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Tidal under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Tidal: Slow Swell Range Slow: a tide of several seconds per cycle with a long rise ( Skew ) opens a filter and the level of a held chord. Tidal: Circular Pan Relation Phase with Spread at maximum: outputs A and B are a sine and a cosine that pan two voices in opposite directions. Tidal: Four Envelopes Mode AD with Relation Harmonic: one trigger gives four envelopes of different lengths on four chord tones. Tidal: Audio Oscillator Range Audio: Tidal is the voice, played from a sequencer; Skew and Smooth drift to change the timbre. Tidal: Clocked Ratios Sync 1 bar with Relation Ratio: four slopes meet again only after several bars and move a filter, a pulse shape and a mix level. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Frequency Slow 0.001–1 Hz, Medium 0.02–50 Hz, Audio 8 Hz – 8 kHz 1 Hz (Medium) Skew 0 – 100 % 50 % Curve −1 … +1 0 Smooth −1 … +1 0 Spread −1 … +1 0 Every knob is a modulation destination. Changing Range keeps the knob's position and the cycle's phase. Settings Setting Values Default Mode AD, Loop, AR Loop Range Slow, Medium, Audio Medium Relation Ratio, Phase, Level, Harmonic Phase Sync Free, 8 bars … 1/32T (straight, dotted, triplet) Free Ratio ÷16, ÷8, ÷6, ÷4, ÷3, ÷2, ×1, ×2, ×3, ×4, ×6, ×8, ×16 ×1 Polarity (Loop) Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. With Transport , Sync still picks a note value or free running. Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig gate AD: starts a slope. AR: high rises and holds, low falls. Loop: a rising edge restarts the cycle Clock trigger follow this clock at Ratio Pitch pitch added to Frequency in octaves Outputs Output Signal What it does A control the main slope B, C, D control related slopes ( Relation , Spread ) Rise gate high while A rises End trigger A finished a cycle or reached 0

title: LFO
text: LFO LFO in the module view Introduction The LFO is a low-frequency oscillator : it moves up and down by itself, slower than you can hear, and makes whatever it's patched into move with it. Patch it onto a filter's cutoff for a sweep, onto an oscillator's pitch for vibrato, or onto a VCA's gain for tremolo. Pick a wave, set the speed, done. It can run freely or lock to the song's bars. How does it work? Speed. With Sync on Free , Rate sets the speed in Hz (cycles per second). Pick a note value in Sync (1/16 … 8 bars) and one cycle takes exactly that long. While the transport plays, a synced LFO follows the song position: it's always at the same point of its wave at the same bar, even after a loop jump, and renders the same every time. When the transport is stopped it keeps running at the synced speed. Waves. Wave chooses what Out plays: Sine and Triangle : smooth up and down. Both start at the middle, rising. Saw Up / Saw Down : a ramp that jumps back at the end of each cycle. Square : high, then low. Pulse Width sets how much of the cycle is high. Random Step : a new random value each cycle, held until the next. Random Smooth : glides from one random value to the next. The Sine , Triangle , Saw , Square and Random outputs give you each wave at once, all at the same speed and phase. Cycle fires a trigger at the start of every cycle. Phase shifts the wave within its cycle. Polarity chooses between Bipolar (−1 … +1, moves both ways around the knob) and Unipolar (0 … 1, only upwards). Random values come from Seed , so they repeat on every render. Reset and Fade. A trigger at Reset restarts the cycle (on a free-running LFO) and the fade-in. With Fade above 0, the output starts at 0 and grows to full over that time after each Reset and each time the transport starts. How to use it? Filter sweep: Out onto a Multi Filter's Cutoff ; set the cable's amount for the depth. Vibrato in a Voice Cell: put the LFO inside the cell, Out onto the oscillator's Pitch knob with a small amount, Voice In › Trigger into Reset , and set Fade to half a second: each note starts straight and then begins to wobble. Rhythmic movement: set Sync to 1/8 and Wave to Square onto a VCA's gain for a tempo-locked chop. Two related movements: use Sine on one destination and Square on another, or two LFOs with Phase 0° and 90° for circular stereo movement. Wobbling the wobble: patch another LFO onto Rate . Clocking other modules: Cycle triggers a sequencer's Clock or an envelope. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 0.01 – 50 Hz 1 Hz Phase 0 – 360° 0° Pulse Width 5 – 95 % 50 % Fade 0 – 10 s 0 s Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Wave Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random Step, Random Smooth Sine Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars Free Polarity Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Seed 0 – 999 1 Inputs Input Signal What it does Reset trigger restarts the cycle (free-running) and the fade-in Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the wave chosen in Wave Sine, Triangle, Saw, Square control each wave, same speed and phase Random control a new random value each cycle, held Cycle trigger a pulse at the start of each cycle

title: Organic LFOs
text: Organic LFOs Organic LFOs in the module view Introduction Organic LFOs are eight slow LFOs that move like a group of living things : related, but never quite in step. Think of a field of grass in the wind, a flock of birds, or eight musicians breathing together without a conductor. One Rate sets the pace, Spread fans the eight speeds apart, and Drift lets each one wander a little in speed and shape, so the pattern never lines up exactly and never sounds mechanical. Yet nothing is left to chance: the wandering comes from the Seed , so every render of your song moves exactly the same way. How does it work? The fan. LFO 1 runs at Rate . With Spread at +1 the others get faster, up to LFO 8 at about 16 times the speed; at −1 they get slower; at 0 all eight share LFO 1's speed. Each LFO also gets a tiny seeded offset, so no two of them settle into a simple, repeating relation. Drift lets every LFO wander along a slow, smooth curve of its own: its speed (at 100 %, between about 21 % slower and 27 % faster) and its shape. A fast LFO wanders faster than a slow one; the wandering always takes a few of its cycles. At 0 % everything is exact. Anchor keeps LFO 1's speed exact (only its shape drifts), so it stays in time with the song while the others float around it. Twist changes the shape of all eight: at −1 soft, rounded plateaus (almost a square), at 0 a sine, at +1 a fast rise to a narrow peak and a long, lazy fall. Drift moves each LFO's twist a little around this. Scatter sets how far apart the eight start after a Reset or a transport start: at 0 % they all start together (and with Spread and Drift at 0, all eight are identical), at 100 % they start anywhere in their cycle. Sum mixes the eight into one complex contour, gently limited. Max follows whichever LFO is highest at the moment: a restless upper outline, mostly in the upper half, great in Unipolar for brightness or density. Level scales every output. Free or locked Free: the LFOs run on their own. Their wandering is counted from the last Reset or transport start, so the same patch rendered from the same start moves the same way. Bars: Rate picks a note value for LFO 1 (64 bars … 1/4T). While the transport plays, everything is worked out from the song position: LFO 1 sits at the same point at the same bar, the others move along their own paths, and jumping around the song (or rendering again) gives exactly the same movement. Drift shifts the phases instead of the speeds here. When the transport stops they run on at the current tempo. Turn Spread while locked and the fan re-forms around the song position, so set it rather than sweep it. Changing the Seed (or the Lock) gives a different group; the outputs fade over 50 ms so it doesn't click. How to use it? Living pad: eight outputs onto the cutoffs, pans or levels of eight voices or layers. Rate 0.05 Hz, Spread +0.4, Drift 40 %. One complex contour: Sum onto a filter or reverb mix: a curve that feels alive but never repeats within a song. Breathing in time: Lock Bars, Rate 4 bars, Anchor on, Drift 30 %: LFO 1 breathes with the bars, the others follow loosely. Brightness that peaks: Max in Unipolar onto a filter cutoff: every time one of the eight peaks, it opens. Different per voice: inside a Voice Cell, add Voice In › Random to Twist or Rate so each note gets its own movement. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Organic LFOs does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Organic LFOs under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Organic LFOs: Living Pad Rate 0.09 Hz and Drift 40 % let four LFOs open and close the filters of a chord while four more move each voice's waveform. Organic LFOs: Breathing in Time Lock on Bars with Anchor : LFO 1 breathes with the song, Max and the others open a filter and pan a plucked line over a light beat. Organic LFOs: Brightness Peaks Max in Unipolar with a high Twist flares the cutoff of a saw arpeggio whenever one of the eight LFOs peaks; Sum widens the reverb. Organic LFOs: Detuned Swarm Each of four saw voices is detuned by its own LFO at a lively rate and high Drift : a restless, chorusing swarm. Organic LFOs: Rain of Tones Twist +1 in Unipolar turns fast LFOs into sharp pulses that gate four bell tones into a never-repeating shower. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 0.002 – 20 Hz, or a note value with Lock = Bars 0.2 Hz Spread −1 … +1 +0.5 Drift 0 – 100 % 30 % Twist −1 … +1 0 Scatter 0 – 100 % 100 % Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Lock Free, Bars Free Anchor On, Off On Polarity Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Seed 0 – 999 1 Inputs Input Signal What it does Reset trigger restarts all eight at their scattered start phases (Free) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 … Out 8 control the eight LFOs, slowest to fastest (Spread ≥ 0) Sum control the eight mixed and soft-limited Max control the highest of the eight

title: Quad LFO
text: Quad LFO Quad LFO in the module view Introduction Quad LFO is four LFOs in one module , with one Mode that decides how they belong together: four free speeds, one speed in four quarter-steps (quadrature), one speed with an adjustable phase spread, or one speed divided into slower and faster related speeds. It's the quickest way to circular stereo movement, rotating pans, four voices that move together but not in unison, or interlocking polyrhythms. Each of the four picks its own wave and depth, and everything can lock to the song's bars. How does it work? Waves. Each LFO has its own Wave : Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square (with the shared Pulse Width ), Random Step and Random Smooth: the same waves as the LFO module. Random values come from Seed and differ per channel, and every render repeats them. Modes. Free: four LFOs, four Rate knobs. Quadrature: one speed ( Rate 1 ), the four a quarter cycle apart: 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°. Two sines a quarter apart draw a circle: patch Out 1 and Out 2 to the X and Y of anything (or to two pans). Phase: like Quadrature, but Spread sets the distance between neighbours (0–360°). At 0° all four move together; at 120° three of them share the cycle evenly; at 180° 1 and 3 match, as do 2 and 4. Divide: one speed, and each LFO runs at its Divide setting of it: ×4, ×3, ×2, ÷1 … ÷8, ÷12, ÷16. With ÷1 ÷2 ÷3 ÷4 they meet again every 12 cycles of LFO 1, and they really do meet: the four restart together whenever their pattern repeats. Switching Mode keeps LFO 1 where it is; the others glide to their new place over 5 ms, so a switch never clicks. Level sets each LFO's depth; a negative level turns it upside down. Polarity chooses −1 … +1 or 0 … 1; in Unipolar, a negative level gives the inverted wave (1 − v) instead of going below 0. Sum is the average of the four. Cycle 1 … 4 fire once per cycle of each LFO, where its wave starts. In Quadrature and Phase they come from LFO 1's cycle, so turning or modulating Spread moves the pulses but never adds extra ones. Timing Free rates: each Rate in Hz (0.01–50 Hz), modulated per sample. Sync on: the Rate knobs pick note values instead (16 bars … 1/32T, straight, dotted and triplet; modulation steps through them). While the transport plays, every LFO is locked to the song position: always at the same point at the same bar, after loop jumps too, and renders repeat. With the transport stopped they run on at the current tempo. Clock: patch a clock and LFO 1 runs one cycle per Clock Ratio pulses, measured from the clock (averaging four pulses) and restarted on every Clock Ratio -th pulse so it stays in step. The other LFOs follow LFO 1 in the shared modes and Divide; in Free mode only LFO 1 follows the clock. After a pause the measurement starts over. Clock wins over Sync. Reset restarts all four (at their offsets in Quadrature and Phase). With Sync on and the transport playing, Reset moves the grid instead: the next sample counts as the start of the cycle, until the transport starts again. A transport start resets everything. Hold freezes all four while it's high and lets them continue where they were. While locked to the song, the outputs freeze and on release jump back to the song position, smoothed over 5 ms. How to use it? Circular panning: Quadrature, Sine on 1 and 2, Out 1 and Out 2 onto two pans (or a mixer's X/Y). Switch the view to XY to see the circle. Four voices, one breath: Phase mode, Spread 90°, the four outputs onto four filter cutoffs in a Voice Cell's neighbours: the same movement, passed along. Polyrhythmic modulation: Divide, Sync on, Rate 1 at 1 bar, Divide ÷1 ÷2 ÷3 ÷4: four movements that line up every twelve bars, on the same bar every time. Random per voice: Free, Random Smooth on all four, slightly different rates: four unrelated, gentle wanderings from one seed. Gating on the beat: a sequencer's clock into Clock , Clock Ratio 4, Square on LFO 1: a chop that follows the clock, even a swung or manual one. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Quad LFO does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Quad LFO under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Quad LFO: Circular Pan Quadrature mode: Out 1 and Out 2 pan two lines in a circle (try the XY view) while Out 3 and Out 4 swell a pad. Quad LFO: Polyrhythm Plucks Divide mode with falling saws at ÷1 ÷2 ÷3 ÷4 pluck the notes of a chord in a 4:3:2 pattern that lines up every twelve beats. Quad LFO: Chord Breath Phase mode with Spread 90° passes one swell along the four voices of a chord, like a breath rolling up and down. Quad LFO: Cycle Drums The Cycle outputs in Divide mode trigger kick, hats, clap and tom at different fractions of one rate: a slowly phasing drum pattern. Quad LFO: Clock Chop A sequencer trigger patched into Clock with Clock Ratio 2 makes a square LFO chop a sustained chord on the grid while LFO 2 sweeps the filter. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 1 0.01 – 50 Hz, or a note value with Sync 1 Hz Rate 2, 3, 4 (Free mode) 0.01 – 50 Hz, or a note value with Sync 1.5, 2, 3 Hz Level 1 … 4 −100 … +100 % 100 % Spread (Phase mode) 0 – 360° 90° Pulse Width 5 – 95 % 50 % Every knob is a modulation destination. title: Neuron
text: Neuron Neuron in the module view Introduction Neuron holds two simple artificial neurons. Each one adds up three weighted inputs, lets the sum charge a leaky "membrane" and fires a gate when the membrane crosses a threshold. The two neurons listen to each other out of the box, so with no cable at all they already play a two-voice rhythm. Patch slow modulation in, or the outputs back into the inputs, and you get rhythms and gestures nobody programmed. How does it work? Sum. Each neuron computes W1 · In 1 + W2 · In 2 + W3 · In 3 . In 1 reads +1 while nothing is patched, so W1 works as a bias knob. In 2 reads 0 while nothing is patched. In 3 hears the other neuron while nothing is patched: its Out or its Gate , chosen with Cross , one sample late. That's a much tighter feedback loop than a cable could make. Membrane. The membrane follows the sum with a delay set by Leak : a short burst at the input moves it a little, a sustained input charges it fully. Leak 0 makes the membrane equal the sum. Gate. In Compare mode the gate is high while the membrane is above the threshold, with Hysteresis as a gap between the on and off levels (no chatter on wobbly inputs). In Spike mode the neuron fires : when the membrane crosses the threshold, the gate goes high for Pulse , the membrane drops to 0 and stays there during the pulse, then charges again. A constant input above the threshold gives a steady rhythm: the higher the input and the shorter the leak, the faster it fires. At or below the threshold it never fires. Out. A smooth version for modulation. In Compare mode it rises from 0 at the threshold with a slope of Sharp , up to 1. In Spike mode the ramp ends at the threshold, so Out shows the membrane charging and drops at each spike: a saw locked to the neuron's rhythm. Sharp 1 is gentle; 100 is almost a gate. Logic. AND , OR and XOR combine the two gates; Diff is A Out − B Out. Neuron has no randomness: the same inputs always give the same outputs. With Reset on Start on, both neurons are cleared when the transport starts, so every render is identical. How to use it? The default rhythm: patch A Spike and B Spike to two drums. A fires regularly from its bias; as A charges, its Out pushes B down, so B fires in irregular gaps. Rhythm from a level: an LFO or envelope into A In 2 : the higher the level, the faster A fires. Velocity to density: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Velocity into In 2 : louder notes fire faster. A Schmitt trigger: A Mode on Compare , a noisy signal into A In 2 , W1 0, Hysteresis up until it stops chattering. Audio: Leak near 0 and Cross on Gate oscillates at audio rate. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Neuron does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Neuron under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Neuron: Self-Made Rhythm Neuron A fires from its bias and its Out inhibits B, so A Spike , B Spike , AND and XOR play kick, snare, clap and hat in an irregular groove. Neuron: Spike Melody B Out is sampled by a quantizer on every A Spike , and spikes ping low pass gates: a pentatonic tune from two cells. Neuron: Accelerando A slow LFO into A In 2 speeds the firing up into a roll and below Threshold silences it; B answers with a tom. Neuron: Audio-Rate Buzz Leak near 0 and Cross on Gate make the pair oscillate at audio rate; an LFO bends W3 and Pulse to retune the buzz. Neuron: Logic Drums Both neurons in Compare mode act as Schmitt triggers on clocked LFOs; AND , XOR , OR and A Gate become kick, clap, hat and snare. Reference Knobs and settings Per neuron (A and B): Control Range Default A / B W1, W2, W3 −2 … +2 A: 0.6, 1, 0.5 · B: 0.9, 1, −1 Threshold −1 … +1 0.5 Hysteresis 0 – 100 % 10 % Leak 0 – 5 s 250 ms / 400 ms Sharp 1 – 100 4 Pulse 1 ms – 1 s 30 ms (Spike mode only) Setting Values Default A Mode, B Mode Compare, Spike Spike Cross Out, Gate, Off Out Reset on Start on / off on W1 … W3: the weight of each input; negative weights inhibit. Threshold: the level the membrane must cross. Drag the dashed line in the view to set it. Hysteresis: the gap between the on and off levels: the gate switches on at Threshold + Hysteresis / 4 and off at Threshold − Hysteresis / 4. Leak: the membrane's time constant. 0 = no delay. Sharp: the slope of Out . Pulse: the gate length in Spike mode, and the time the membrane rests after firing. Cross: what In 3 hears from the other neuron while unpatched. Reset on Start: clear both neurons when the transport starts. All knobs are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does A In 1, B In 1 control weighted by W1; unpatched: +1 A In 2, B In 2 control weighted by W2; unpatched: 0 A In 3, B In 3 control weighted by W3; unpatched: the other neuron (see Cross ) Reset trigger clears both membranes and ends any spike Outputs Output Signal What it does A Gate, B Gate gate the neuron's firing state A Out, B Out control, 0 … 1 the sharpened membrane A Spike, B Spike trigger a pulse each time the gate goes high AND, OR, XOR gate logic of A Gate and B Gate Diff control, −1 … +1 A Out − B Out

title: Random
text: Random Random in the module view Introduction Random produces a new random value on every step: the classic stepped "sample and hold" modulation. What makes it musical is its memory . The Loop knob moves it from always new values, through a pattern that slowly changes, to a fixed loop that repeats exactly. Every value comes from a seed, so a patch sounds the same every time you play it back. How does it work? Steps. Random moves to its next value on each step. Where the steps come from, in order of priority: Clock input patched: every rising edge at Clock is a step. Sync set to a note value: one step per note value at Live's tempo. While the transport plays, the steps are locked to the song position. Sync on Free: steps run at Rate , in Hz. Each new step fires a pulse at Trig . Memory. The values sit in a loop of Length slots. Each time the loop comes round, every slot gets a new value with a probability of 1 − Loop , and otherwise keeps the old one: Loop 0 %: every step is new. Pure randomness. Loop 50 %: about half of the values change each pass. A pattern that evolves. Loop 100 %: nothing changes. A locked sequence of Length steps. The values are a function of the seed and the step number, not of what came before. With Sync on and the transport running, the step number comes from the song position, so a section always plays the same values, even if you start playback in the middle. Starting the transport restarts the sequence. Shaping. Each raw value is scaled to Bias ± Spread and clipped to −1 … +1. Semitones rounds it to steps of 1/12 (one semitone at 1 V/oct). Smooth glides from one value to the next instead of jumping. How to use it? Random modulation: patch Out onto a filter's cutoff or an oscillator's shape. Set the depth with the cable's amount. Melodies: turn on Semitones , lower Spread (e.g. 25 % = ±3 semitones), patch Out into an Oscillator's Pitch and Trig into an ADSR's gate. Keep the cable amount at 100 % so the notes stay on semitones. Raise Loop until you like the phrase, then set it to 100 % to keep it. Find a different phrase: change Seed . Each seed is its own sequence. Play in time with something else: patch a clock or a gate into Clock , e.g. a Function's EOC or a sequencer's gate. Wandering, smooth modulation: raise Smooth for drifting values instead of steps. At 100 % the value glides over most of a step. Only positive values: set Bias to +0.5 and Spread to 50 % for 0 … 1. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Rate 0.05 – 50 Hz 2 Hz Spread 0 – 100 % 100 % Bias −1 … +1 0 Smooth 0 – 100 % 0 % Loop 0 – 100 % 0 % Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars 1/4 Length 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32 steps 8 steps Semitones on / off off Seed 0 – 999 1 Rate: steps per second. Only used when Sync is Free and Clock is not patched. Spread: the width of the range. At 100 % values cover −1 … +1 (around Bias ); at 0 % every value equals Bias . Bias: the centre of the range. Values beyond ±1 are clipped, so a high bias with a wide spread makes values stick to the top. Smooth: glide between values, as a share of the step length. 0 % jumps; higher values slide. The glide follows the step length, so it works the same at any rate or tempo. Loop: the chance that a slot keeps its value when the loop comes round. 0 % always new, 100 % locked. Sync: Free steps at Rate . A note value sets one step per note at Live's tempo (4/4 assumed). Ignored while Clock is patched. Length: the number of slots in the loop. It sets how long a locked pattern is before it repeats. Semitones: rounds each value to the nearest 1/12, i.e. to semitones for pitch inputs. The rounding happens before Smooth , so gliding still slides between the notes. Seed: picks the sequence. The same seed always gives the same values. Rate , Spread , Bias , Smooth and Loop are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock gate when patched, every rising edge advances one step; overrides Rate and Sync Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control, −1 … +1 the current value Trig trigger one pulse on every new step

title: Uncertainty
text: Uncertainty Uncertainty in the module view Introduction Uncertainty is six random generators in one module, each with a different character: two Fluctuating voltages that wander continuously, two Quantized voltages that jump between a few levels, a Stored value whose distribution you can skew and whose values can depend on each other, and an Integrated voltage that turns the stored values into random slopes. Whenever something in a patch should move unpredictably, one of these six probably fits. How does it work? Fluctuating 1 and 2 are smooth curves through random points. In Free mode the points come on average every 1 / Rate seconds, irregularly spaced so there is no audible pulse. With F Sync on a note value and the transport playing, the points sit on the grid and the curve is a function of the song position. Spread sets the size. The two have different default rates, so they rarely move together. Quantized 1 and 2 jump on each clock to one of 2, 4, 8 or 16 levels ( Bits 1 … 4). With Interval Even the levels spread evenly over 0 … 1 (1 bit is a random on/off voltage). With an interval in semitones each level is that many semitones above the last: 3 bits with 7 semitones jumps between eight notes a fifth apart. Few levels give a small vocabulary the ear hears as a pattern. Quantized 2 has its own Clock Q2 input; while it's unpatched it follows Quantized 1's clock divided by Q2 Divide . Stored takes a new value on each Store event. Three controls shape it: Correlation: how much each value depends on the previous one. 0 %: independent. Positive: each value stays near the last, a slow stepped wander. Negative: values alternate high and low, a zig-zag. The overall spread of values stays the same. Shape: Uniform , Bell (values gather in the middle) or Edges (values are pushed outward). Distribution: skews the values toward the top (+) or the bottom (−). Integrated uses Stored as a slope: it rises while Stored is positive and falls while it's negative, at a speed set by Integrate , and bounces back from ±1. The result is a line that changes direction and speed at every Store event. With positive Correlation it makes long sweeps; with negative Correlation it trembles around a point. Clocks. Each clock follows its input when patched, else the song position when its Sync is on a note value (at the synced length while the transport is stopped), else its Rate . A synced Fluctuating curve holds while the transport is stopped. Repeatable. Every value comes from Seed . Synced generators are a function of the song position and render the same from any start; the free ones and Integrated render the same from the same start. How to use it? Slow, organic movement: Fluct 1 and Fluct 2 to two filter cutoffs or pans. A small random melody: Quant 1 with Q1 Interval 2 semitones and 3 bits into an oscillator's pitch, Q Sync 1/8. Random octaves: Q2 Interval 12, Q2 Bits 2. A random on/off switch: 1 bit on Quantized 2, Q2 Divide /4. A drifting value per note: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Trigger into Store , Correlation +80 %: each note's value is near the last one. Random sweeps: Integrated to a filter cutoff, Correlation +60 %. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Uncertainty does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Uncertainty under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Uncertainty: Random Melody Quant 1 with Q1 Bits 3 and Q1 Interval 2 st, snapped to D minor pentatonic by a quantizer, plays an endless random tune. Uncertainty: Drifting Pad Fluct 1 and Fluct 2 at different rates move the filters, waveforms and pans of a four-voice pad. Uncertainty: Random Sweeps Stored with Correlation +65 % feeds Integrated , a random sweep on the cutoff of an arpeggio; a one-bit Quant 2 switches the hats. Uncertainty: Random Octaves Q2 Interval 12 st sends a fixed riff to random octaves and a one-bit Quant 1 at 7 st adds fifths. Uncertainty: Drunken Walk Stored with Correlation +85 % and Shape Bell wanders pitch step by step; a quantizer and pinged gates turn it into bells. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default F1 Rate, F2 Rate 0.01 – 20 Hz 0.5 Hz, 0.17 Hz F1 Spread, F2 Spread 0 – 100 % 100 % Q Rate 0.05 – 40 Hz 2 Hz Store Rate 0.05 – 40 Hz 1 Hz Distribution −100 … +100 % 0 % Correlation −95 … +95 % 0 % Integrate 0.01 – 10 /s 0.5 /s F Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars Free Q Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars 1/8 Store Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars 1/4 Q1 Bits, Q2 Bits 1 – 4 3, 2 Q1 Interval, Q2 Interval Even, 1, 2, 5, 7, 12 st Even Q2 Divide /1, /2, /3, /4, /8 /2 Shape Uniform, Bell, Edges Uniform Seed 0 – 999 1 F Rate: the average number of points per second of a Fluctuating curve (Free mode). Changing it stretches the curve; it never jumps. F Spread: the size of a Fluctuating output. Q Rate / Store Rate: the free clocks of Quantized 1 and Stored (shown while their Sync is Free ). Distribution, Correlation, Shape: shape Stored (see above). Integrate: the speed of Integrated per unit of Stored. Bits: 2^Bits levels. Interval: Even spreads them over 0 … 1; semitones stack them at 1 V/oct. Q2 Divide: while Clock Q2 is unpatched, Quantized 2 steps on every n-th step of Quantized 1. Seed: one seed; each generator has its own stream of it. All knobs are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock Q1 trigger each pulse steps Quantized 1 Clock Q2 trigger each pulse steps Quantized 2; unpatched: Quantized 1's clock / Q2 Divide Store trigger each pulse takes a new Stored value Outputs Output Signal What it does Fluct 1, Fluct 2 control, −1 … +1 continuously wandering voltages Quant 1, Quant 2 control (0 … 1, or 1 V/oct) stepped random on 2^Bits levels Stored control, −1 … +1 the stored value Integrated control, −1 … +1 random slopes from the stored values Store Trig trigger a pulse when Stored takes a new value

title: Wobble
text: Wobble Wobble in the module view Introduction Wobble turns one stream of random values into three shapes of movement. Stepped jumps to each new value, Smooth glides to it, and Wobble glides with momentum: it overshoots, wobbles around the value and settles. Patch them to related destinations (Stepped to pitch, Wobble to the filter) and the movements belong together. Around them sit bursts of quick triggers, a step clock, a Compare gate and a Chaos knob that feeds the module back into itself. How does it work? Steps. Wobble takes a new random value on each step. Steps come from: Clock patched: every rising edge. Sync on a note value: one step per note value. While the transport plays the steps are locked to the song position. Sync on Free: steps at Rate . Each step fires Clock . With Sample patched, each step samples that signal instead of taking a random value: a sample and hold with three output shapes. While Hold is high no new values are taken (and Clock stays quiet), but Smooth and Wobble keep settling. Smooth follows Stepped through a smooth low-pass filter. Smooth sets how slowly: at 0 % it almost jumps, at 50 % it arrives just in time for the next step, at 100 % it barely moves before the next value comes. The filter follows the step length, so the character is the same at any rate or tempo. Wobble uses the same filter with resonance. Wobble 0 % behaves like Smooth; higher values overshoot each new value and ring around it. When the next step comes before it settles, the wobbles overlap: that's where the bouncing comes from. Beyond ±1 the output is softly limited to ±1.5. Burst. On each step, with the chance Burst , a burst of 2 … Burst Size quick triggers fires over the first half of the step: rolls for drums or quick re-triggers of an envelope. Compare is high while Stepped is above Smooth: an irregular gate whose rhythm follows the movement. Chaos feeds the module back into itself. The new values are bent toward the current Smooth value and folded, so above about 40 % they cluster, run in streaks and break away. In Free mode fast wobbles also speed up the steps, and burst spacing gets irregular. Steps that follow the song position stay on the grid. Repeatable. The random values come from Seed and the step number. With Chaos at 0 and Sync on a note value, Stepped is a function of the song position. With Chaos up, a render from the same start position is always identical. How to use it? Three related movements: Stepped to an oscillator's pitch (through a quantizer), Wobble to the filter cutoff, Smooth to the pan. Bouncy filter: Wobble 80 %, Smooth 40 %, Sync 1/8, into a filter's cutoff. Slow drift: Smooth 100 %, Rate 0.1 Hz: a wandering line. One value per note: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Trigger into Clock : every note gets a new value that wobbles into place. Drum rolls: Burst into a drum's trigger, Burst 30 %, Sync 1/4. A sample and hold: patch a signal into Sample and a clock into Clock . Demo patches Five whole patches show what Wobble does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Wobble under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Wobble: Wandering Melody Stepped picks a new pitch every eighth through a Quantizer in D Dorian while Wobble springs the filter open; try Chaos and Smooth . Wobble: Bouncy Bass The Wobble output with a high Wobble amount bounces a ladder filter on a bass line at Sync 1/8. Wobble: Burst Rolls Burst fires quick rolls into a tom, Stepped retunes it and Compare opens the hats; raise Burst and Burst Size . Wobble: Drifting Pad At a slow Rate with Smooth at 100 %, the outputs drift a filter, pulse width and pitch of a held chord. Wobble: Sampled Arp A slow triangle LFO in Sample is read on every 1/16, so Stepped draws a staircase that a Quantizer turns into an arpeggio. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Rate 0.02 – 40 Hz 1 Hz Smooth 0 – 100 % 50 % Wobble 0 – 100 % 60 % Chaos 0 – 100 % 0 % Burst 0 – 100 % 25 % Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars Free Burst Size 2 – 8 4 Polarity Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Seed 0 – 999 1 Rate: steps per second, when Sync is Free and Clock is unpatched. Smooth: how slowly Smooth and Wobble follow the steps. Wobble: the resonance of the Wobble output. Chaos: feedback from the outputs into the values, the clock and the bursts. Burst: the chance of a burst on each step. Level: the size of Stepped, Smooth and Wobble. Burst Size: the most pulses a burst can have. Polarity: Bipolar −1 … +1, Unipolar 0 … 1. Seed: picks the sequence of values. Rate , Smooth , Wobble , Chaos , Burst and Level are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse is a step; overrides Rate and Sync Sample control when patched, each step samples it instead of a random value Hold gate while high, no new values and no Clock pulses Outputs Output Signal What it does Stepped control the current value Smooth control the values, glided without overshoot Wobble control the values, glided with overshoot and ringing (±1.5 at most) Burst trigger clusters of quick pulses Clock trigger one pulse per step Compare gate high while Stepped is above Smooth

title: Chart Recorder
text: Chart Recorder Introduction Chart Recorder is a pen drawing a signal onto a looping strip of paper; the strip plays back as modulation. The pen is a heavy, sprung mechanism: it lags, overshoots, sticks and bangs into its end stops, so even a plain envelope comes out with character, live at Pen . The strip replays at another speed, backwards, locked to the song or scrubbed by hand, and you can draw on the paper with the mouse. How does it work? Detector. In goes through Gain into the detector, which decides what the pen draws: DC: the signal itself, −1 … +1. For control signals. Rectified, RMS: the average level, smoothed over Response . Peak: jumps up at once and falls back over Response . Log dB: the RMS level in decibels, like a level recorder: 0 dBFS at the top edge, − Log Range at the bottom. Audio into In is fine with the level detectors. With DC, Pen and Replay are bipolar (−1 … +1); with the others they are unipolar (0 … 1). The pen is a weight on a spring with a damper. Writing Speed is how fast it can move and how stiff the spring is: fast, it follows closely; slow, it draws straight ramps between levels. Damping low makes it overshoot and wiggle around each new level; high makes it creep. Friction makes it stick: small changes don't move it until they add up (up to 4 % of the paper width), so smooth movement turns into small steps. At the edges of the paper the pen hits its end stops and bounces back a little: an overdriven input draws flattened tops with a small kick. Pen always carries the pen's position, whether it is writing or not. There is no randomness: the same input draws the same line. Paper. The strip is Length long and loops. With Paper on Transport it moves with the song (1 … 64 bars) and stands still while the transport is stopped; on Free it runs all the time (1 s … 10 min), at Paper Speed . Hold Paper (the input or the button) stops the paper while the pen keeps writing into the same spot; in Transport mode the paper rejoins the song when you let go. The strip keeps 200 points per second (coarser beyond 2 minutes). Changing Length resamples it; a tempo change stretches it with the song. Recording. Record decides when the pen writes: Always: whenever the paper moves. Gate: while the Record input is high. Armed: a rising edge on Record (or the Arm button) arms; writing starts when the paper next comes round to the start, and stops after exactly one pass. The view shows Armed, Writing and Done. Writing replaces what was on the paper. Clear (input or button) wipes the strip and its marks. Mark puts a tick on the paper edge where the pen is. Replay. The replay head reads the strip at Replay Speed : 1× is the paper's own speed, negative runs backwards, 0 parks it. With Replay Sync on Song its position follows the song position (it holds while stopped); on Free it runs on its own and Reset sends it back to the start (to Offset ). Offset is added to the head, so with Replay Speed at 0 it scrubs through the strip. Interpolation reads between points: Step holds each point, Linear draws lines, Smooth draws curves. Unwritten paper reads the last ink before it; an empty strip reads 0. Marker fires whenever the replay head passes a mark, in either direction. Position is the replay head, 0 at the start of the strip and 1 at the end. Drawing. In the view, drag on the paper to draw ink, Shift-drag for one straight line, right-drag to erase and Alt-click to add or remove a mark. Each drag is one undo step. The strip is saved with the board; what the module records is saved too (when recording stops, after each pass and every few seconds while writing). How to use it? A character envelope: an ADSR into In , Writing Speed 30 mm/s, Damping 20 %: Pen is the envelope with momentum, overshoot and ringing. Sticky steps: a slow LFO into In , Friction 70 %: Pen moves in irregular little steps. Record a gesture, play it back: a Dial into In , Record on Armed, press Arm and move the dial for one pass. Replay loops it in time with the song; set Replay Speed to −1 to play it backwards or 0.5 for half speed. A level follower: a drum bus into In , Detector Log dB, Response 100 ms: Replay gives the loop's loudness contour, ready for ducking or filter moves. A scrubbed table: Replay Speed 0 and a modulation source into Offset : the strip becomes a drawn transfer curve. Events from the drawing: Alt-click marks onto the paper and patch Marker into an envelope's trigger. Inside a Voice Cell: every voice has its own pen and replay head; only the first voice records. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Chart Recorder does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Chart Recorder under Demos by module ; loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Chart Recorder: Pen with Momentum A bass envelope drawn with low Damping and slow Writing Speed overshoots, and the pen wobble sweeps the filter. Chart Recorder: Sticky Steps High Friction turns slow LFOs into irregular steps that a Quantizer plays as a melody. Chart Recorder: Backwards Gesture A live random walk is recorded on a four-bar strip, and a second voice plays it back with Replay Speed −1. Chart Recorder: Loudness Contour Detector Log dB draws the drum loop's level, and an inverted Pen ducks a pad on every kick. Chart Recorder: Drawn Table A drawn curve with Replay Speed 0 is scrubbed by Offset , so the drawing becomes a looping melody. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Gain −24 … +24 dB 0 dB Response 1 ms – 2 s 50 ms Writing Speed 1 – 1000 mm/s 100 mm/s Damping 0 – 100 % 70 % Friction 0 – 100 % 0 % Paper Speed 0.25 – 4× 1× Replay Speed −4 … +4× +1× Offset 0 – 100 % 0 % Detector DC, Rectified, RMS, Peak, Log dB DC Log Range 10, 25, 50, 75 dB 50 dB Paper Free, Transport Transport Length (Free) 1 s, 2 s, 5 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min, 5 min, 10 min 10 s Length (Transport) 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 bars 4 bars Record Always, Gate, Armed Gate Replay Sync Free, Song Song Interpolation Step, Linear, Smooth Linear Gain: the input level before the detector. Response: the averaging time of Rectified, RMS and Log dB; the fall time of Peak. Writing Speed: the fastest the pen moves; also its stiffness. Damping: low overshoots and wiggles, high creeps. Friction: how much change it takes to move the pen. Paper Speed: the paper's speed in Free mode (only shown there). Replay Speed: the replay head's speed; negative runs backwards. Offset: shifts the replay head along the strip. Log Range: the span of the paper with the Log dB detector (only shown then). The eight knobs are modulation destinations. The Clear , Arm and Hold Paper buttons act like the inputs (Hold Paper toggles). Inputs Input Signal What it does In control the signal to draw (audio is fine with the level detectors) Record gate writes while high (Gate); a rising edge arms one pass (Armed) Mark trigger puts a mark on the paper at the pen Hold Paper gate stops the paper while high Clear trigger wipes the strip and its marks Reset trigger sends the replay head back to Offset (Replay Sync Free) Outputs Output Signal What it does Pen control the live pen position, writing or not Replay control the strip, read at the replay head Marker trigger a pulse whenever the replay head passes a mark Position control the replay head, 0 … 1 along the strip

title: Envelope Follower
text: Envelope Follower Envelope Follower in the module view Introduction The Envelope Follower turns how loud a signal is into a smooth control signal. Patch a drum loop or a voice in, and the Env output rises with every hit and falls back between them, ready to move a filter, a VCA or anything else. It works on audio and on CV alike: followed CV becomes a slew limiter with separate rise and fall times. For a meter with bars and a clip light use the Level Meter ; the Envelope Follower is the tool when you want the shape of the signal, with your own attack and release. How does it work? The detector looks at the size of each sample. When the signal gets bigger than the current envelope, the envelope rises with the Attack time; when it gets smaller, it falls with the Release time. Times are the time to cover 63 % of the way, as on any one-pole smoother. Short attack and release follow every wave; a short attack with a long release follows the peaks of a drum pattern. Detector picks how the size is measured: Peak follows the absolute value of the signal (or one half of it, see Rectify ): fast and punchy. RMS follows the average power: smoother and closer to how loud the signal sounds. Attack and Release apply to the power, and Rectify has no effect. Gain multiplies the result, so a quiet source can still reach 1. The Gate output opens when Env reaches Threshold and closes again when it falls under 80 % of it, so a hovering level does not chatter. Trigger sends one short pulse every time the gate opens. How to use it? Ducking: a kick into In , Inverted into a VCA's Gain on the pad. A short attack and a release of 150–300 ms gives the pump. Loudness to brightness: Env into a filter's Cutoff . Audio to triggers: a drum loop into In , Trigger into another module's trigger input: it plays on every hit above Threshold . Slew a CV: set Rectify to None (signed) and patch a stepped CV in: Env follows it with Attack going up and Release going down, and Inverted is the same signal upside down. Only the positive part of an LFO: Rectify = Positive . Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Attack 0 – 2 s 10 ms Release 0 – 5 s 200 ms Gain 0 – 8 × 1 × Threshold 0 – 100 % 30 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Detector Peak, RMS Peak Rectify (Peak only) Full, Positive, Negative, None (signed) Full Inputs Input Signal What it does In audio the signal to follow; control signals work as well Outputs Output Signal What it does Env control the followed level times Gain ; with None (signed) it can go negative Inverted control 1 − Env , limited to 0…1; with None (signed) , − Env Gate gate high from Threshold up (closes at 80 % of it) Trigger trigger one sample when the gate opens

title: Dual Filter
text: Dual Filter Dual Filter in the module view Introduction The Dual Filter is two multimode filters under one Cutoff . A Spread knob pulls their cutoffs apart, symmetrically around the centre. Routed in series, in parallel or one per stereo channel, the pair becomes a band-pass with two independent edges, a vowel-like two-peak formant filter, a band-reject, or a stereo filter whose left and right sit at different frequencies. One cable on Cutoff moves both filters; one on Spread opens and closes the gap. Use the Multi Filter when you want a particular character (ladders, shelves, phasers). Use the Dual Filter for shapes that need two filters working together. How does it work? Both filters are zero-delay-feedback state-variable filters (12 dB/oct), the same as the Multi Filter's SVF Multimode and SVF Saturating (Rough) . They stay in tune and click-free under fast modulation, even at audio rate. Cutoff is the centre between the two cutoffs. Spread is their distance in octaves: at +2 oct and 1 kHz, filter 1 sits at 500 Hz and filter 2 at 2 kHz. Negative Spread puts filter 2 below filter 1.
